subject: Risk allocation & prepaid transition plan — review of LoL carve-outs
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Katy Lewis <katy@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Risk allocation & prepaid transition plan — review of LoL carve-outs

Katy / Mark — thanks again for the productive call this morning. Attached are our current MSA and the Order Form with the redlines that came out of legal and finance (MSA_v3_redline.pdf, OrderForm_Acme_v2.docx). Two specific areas we need alignment on before we move to signature:

1) Limitation of Liability carve-outs: Acme is asking for an explicit carve-out for consequential damages and for a broader negligence carve-out tied to wind-down assistance. We are comfortable with carve-outs for gross negligence and intentional misconduct, but need to avoid an open-ended consequential damages exposure.

2) Prepaid fees and termination / wind-down interplay: Order Form currently shows a six-month prepayment. Acme wants either a full refund on termination for convenience plus wind-down assistance or a short pro-rata refund and a 90-day transition. Finance is nervous about a full refund combined with unlimited wind-down assistance.

Quick asks: can Rishi and Katy weigh in on two options below and tell us which is acceptable to Acme?
- Option A (Preferred by Redwood): Carve-out for gross negligence and willful misconduct only; cap remains lesser of 12 months of fees or total prepaid balance; on termination for convenience, offer pro-rata refund for unused time minus any documented wind-down fees (capped).
- Option B (Compromise): Add limited carve-out for negligent data handling leading to direct customer damages (not consequential) and increase cap to the greater of prepaid remaining balance or 6 months of fees; offer up to 30 days of wind-down assistance at no charge, additional assistance billed.

We'd like legal redline guidance by end of business Monday (2/23) so we can finalize the Order Form for signature.

Thanks —
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Katy Lewis <katy@acmeanalytics.com>

Date: Sat, 21 Feb 2026 10:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Risk allocation & prepaid transition plan — review of LoL carve-outs

Aditya / team — thanks for the summary and the documents. High level thoughts from Acme Legal:

- Consequential damages carve-out: we understand Redwood's exposure concerns. Acme cannot accept an absolute bar on consequential damages given our downstream SLA commitments to our customers. We would accept a mutual carve-out limited by a specified list (e.g., loss of business, lost profits) but with an exception for data loss that is a direct result of Redwood’s negligence.

- Gross negligence vs. negligence: Acme will not accept limiting recovery only to gross negligence for incidents involving customer data. For data breaches or loss we need a lower threshold (ordinary negligence) to be actionable, but we are willing to limit recoverable damages to direct, provable losses.

- Prepaid refunds and wind-down: Acme needs a firm guarantee of a refund for unused prepaid periods upon termination for convenience unless the parties agree to a documented wind-down plan that explicitly lists services and fees. A unilateral deduction for wind-down "costs" is too open-ended; any deduction should be itemized and mutually agreed.

We appreciate Redwood offering a cap tied to prepaid balance; that is constructive. Instead of months-of-fees formulas, can we propose a defined cap equal to the remaining prepaid balance plus documented out-of-pocket wind-down costs (subject to maximum of remaining prepaid balance)? That keeps the math clear for our CFO.

I'll circulate more specific redline language on Monday morning.

— Katy
Katy Lewis
Senior Counsel, Acme Analytics
katy@acmeanalytics.com

Referenced attachments: inline comments in MSA_v3_redline.pdf

Katy — appreciate the quick response and the clarity. A few points from Redwood Legal after internal review: we want to balance clarity for Acme with protecting Redwood’s service-level economics. Proposed positions below; I’ve also included suggested redline snippets in the attached MSA (MSA_v3_redline.pdf).

1) Limitation of liability language:
- We will accept an express carve-out removing liability limitations for: (i) claims arising from Redwood's willful misconduct or gross negligence; and (ii) claims arising from Redwood's negligence that result in material data loss (as defined). For other negligence-based claims (e.g., routine outages), recovery will be limited to direct damages capped as set forth below.
- Consequential damages remain excluded, but we are willing to add a narrowly drawn exception for a defined list of downstream losses if those losses are direct and reasonably foreseeable and caused by Redwood’s breach (example list: third-party regulatory fines, direct lost revenue).

Redline suggestion (excerpt):
"Notwithstanding the foregoing, neither party shall be liable for consequential, incidental, special, exemplary, or punitive damages except where such damages arise from (a) gross negligence or willful misconduct, or (b) verified direct losses resulting from proven material data loss caused by the other party's negligent acts, subject to the caps set forth in Section X."

2) Cap and prepaid interplay:
- We propose the cap for direct damages be the lesser of (i) twelve (12) months of fees actually paid under the Order Form, or (ii) the total remaining prepaid balance at the time of the loss. This ties the cap both to contract economics and the prepaid amount.
- For termination for convenience: offer pro-rata refund of unused prepaid fees, less documented, mutually agreed wind-down expenses. To avoid disputes, wind-down expenses must be pre-approved in a transition plan (a short exhibit to the Order Form) and subject to a maximum percentage (we propose 15% of the unused balance as a default, unless otherwise agreed).

Alternate narrow compromise (if Acme cannot accept 12 months): cap at remaining prepaid balance (simpler) and commit to 30 days of no-charge wind-down assistance; additional transition work invoiced at standard rates.

Next steps: If Acme can accept either the 12-month-limited cap or the remaining-prepaid-balance cap plus 30-day assistance, we can prepare a clean MSA and a short transition exhibit for signature.

Thanks —
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com

Katy / Mark — thanks for the detailed feedback and for being constructive on the cap mechanics. Internal alignment here; we think the narrow compromise below will get us across the finish line without exposing Redwood to open-ended risk. Proposed final terms for Acme review: 

- Cap: the parties agree that direct damages will be capped at the lesser of (i) twelve (12) months of fees paid under the Order Form, or (ii) the remaining prepaid balance at the time of the claim.
- Carve-outs: carve-outs from the Limitation of Liability for willful misconduct and gross negligence will remain. Additionally, carve-outs will apply to negligence leading to verified material data loss (defined in an exhibit), but consequential damages remain excluded except for a narrowly defined list of direct downstream regulatory fines and direct lost revenue that are reasonably foreseeable.
- Termination and prepaid refunds: on termination for convenience, Redwood will provide a pro-rata refund of unused prepaid fees. Deductions for wind-down assistance must be documented and mutually agreed in a short transition exhibit; Redwood will cover up to 30 days of basic wind-down assistance at no additional charge. If the parties cannot agree on wind-down costs within 10 business days, Redwood will issue the pro-rata refund and the parties will resolve wind-down reconciliation post-termination through the dispute resolution process.

If Acme can confirm acceptance of these bullets, Rishi will prepare a clean MSA and a one-page Transition Exhibit to attach to the Order Form and we will route for signature (DocuSign link attached). If you prefer the alternative (cap = remaining prepaid balance and 30-day assistance), say so and we will mark accordingly.

Proposed next steps: please respond by EOD Thursday (2/26) so we can finish procurement and finance sign-off.

Best,
